scenes.vo: Every Sunday at nine, a wrong number calls me. An old woman. She always asks, beta, did you eat?
scenes.cap: Every Sunday 9 PM, a wrong number: "Beta, did you eat?"

scenes.vo: The first time, I said, aunty, wrong number. She said sorry, and hung up. Next Sunday, she called again.
scenes.cap: "Aunty, wrong number." Next Sunday, she called again.

scenes.vo: I had just moved to a new city. No friends. Nobody else was asking if I'd eaten.
scenes.cap: New city. No friends. Nobody else asked if I'd eaten.

scenes.vo: So the third Sunday, I said, yes Maa, I ate. She talked for twenty minutes. About her plants. Her knees. Her neighbour's dog.
scenes.cap: Third Sunday: "Yes Maa, I ate." 20 minutes about her plants.

scenes.vo: Months passed. Then one Sunday she said, I know you're not my son. My son stopped calling. You didn't.
scenes.cap: "I know you're not my son. My son stopped calling. You didn't."

scenes.vo: Last week she gave me her address. This Sunday I'm going there with food. Because this time, I want to be the one who asks. Maa, did you eat?
scenes.cap: This Sunday I'll ask: "Maa, did you eat?"
